name: Severe Neurodevelopmental Disorder-Facial Dysmorphism-Cerebral-Renal-Cardiac Anomalies Syndrome
aliases: Severe Neurodevelopmental and Multisystem Dysmorphic Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for SNFCRCA Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic facial dysmorphic features including hypertelorism, broad nasal bridge, and micrognathia
Severe global developmental delay or intellectual disability evident in infancy or early childhood
Congenital cerebral anomalies (e.g. ventriculomegaly), renal malformations (e.g. renal hypoplasia), and cardiac defects (e.g. septal defects)
Postnatal growth retardation or failure to thrive
Identification of pathogenic variant in associated gene(s) if known

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria (facial dysmorphism, neurodevelopmental delay, and multisystem anomalies)
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic etiology remains to be fully elucidated; diagnosis primarily clinical and supported by imaging and genetic testing when available.

pathognomonic.notes: Marked impairment in multiple developmental domains

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic facial dysmorphism (hypertelorism, broad nasal bridge, micrognathia)
searchTerms: wide spaced eyes, broad nose, small jaw
facial features with hypertelorism and micrognathia

pathognomonic.notes: Including atrial and ventricular septal defects
searchTerms: holes in heart walls present at birth

common.notes: Structural kidney anomalies detected on imaging

common.symptomName: Ventriculomegaly or other cerebral structural anomalies
common.notes: Detected by brain MRI or ultrasound
Failure to thrive in infancy and early childhood

occasional.symptomName: Skeletal anomalies including clinodactyly or joint contractures

rare.notes: Likely secondary to hypotonia or aspiration

laboratory: Normal metabolic screening in most cases
Occasional hypothyroidism detected by thyroid function tests
imaging: Brain MRI showing ventriculomegaly and cerebral malformations
Renal ultrasound demonstrating hypoplasia or dysplasia

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of pachygyria and iris coloboma
Distinctive brain malformations with known ACTB/ACTG1 mutations
More severe renal cystic dysplasia and perinatal lethality

redFlags: Severe global developmental delay with multisystem involvement
Congenital cardiac defects requiring early intervention
Renal anomalies with risk of progressive renal insufficiency
references: Orphanet: Severe neurodevelopmental disorder-facial dysmorphism-cerebral-renal-cardiac anomalies syndrome, ORPHA:708166
